title: Most important predictors of father-child contact in the U.S. child welfare system: A machine learning approach.
summary: Specific learned observational result about survey-record missingness and contact prediction, beyond generic algorithm accuracy. Acknowledges recording-process dominance, adaptive test tuning and noncausal scope.
ai_technology: Machine-learning models for father–child contact prediction in child-welfare records
organization: The Ohio State University College of Social Work

evidence.tested: Specific learned observational result about survey-record missingness and contact prediction, beyond generic algorithm accuracy. Acknowledges recording-process dominance, adaptive test tuning and noncausal scope.
evidence.unknown: The reported evaluation does not establish prospective benefit or performance beyond the studied setting.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts father–child contact from U.S. child-welfare survey data; the paper identifies record missingness and documentation patterns as major predictors.
